fact: TechTrends KE reports the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, with inaugural commissioner Immaculate Kassait in office since 2020 and a Senior Deputy Data Commissioner serving; the Public Service Commission shortlisted 13 of 152 applicants to succeed her.
The Star reports the ODPC as the independent oversight body established by the Act and acting, with a registration register and notice of 28 August 2026.
The Standard reports that Data Commissioner Immaculate Kassait led the ODPC's launch of an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system on 14 July 2026, showing the office constituted and acting.
The Nation reports the ODPC as tasked with overseeing compliance and having identified 224 gaming and betting firms handling minors' data, as stated to the Senate on 13 May 2026.

Cadmus Cyber Solutions states that, as at September 2024, the ODPC had fined at least nine businesses a total of KES 26,275,000 under the Data Protection Act and Regulations, including Oppo Kenya (2022, KES 5m) and SBM Bank (2024, KES 450,000).
Cadmus Cyber Solutions states the ODPC investigates complaints and has fined at least nine businesses between 2022 and September 2024.

The ODPC bulletin states that as of March 2025 the Office had received 7,128 complaints and resolved 97 percent, issued 215 determinations, imposed penalties on 10 entities, issued 103 compensations and settled 39 other cases through ADR (a cumulative count, no single year stated).

The bulletin shows the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner acting under Data Commissioner Immaculate Kassait, with offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru, registering data handlers and investigating complaints within 90 days.
